title: No. 1 — where they decided what was still blank
subtopic: T11 — the Royal Geographical Society, six doors away
learning_goal: Know that the RGS ran the era's exploration from the top of Fogg's own street, and feel the irony against a man who crosses the world without looking at it.

narration.script: At the top of Fogg's street is the room where Britain worked out which parts of the world were still unmapped. The Royal Geographical Society moved into number one Savile Row in eighteen seventy, from Burlington House round the corner — and this street was built on the Burlington estate, so it was a move of a few hundred yards. That is the room where expeditions to Africa, Asia and the South Pole were planned and argued over. In April eighteen seventy-four, David Livingstone's body lay in that building before it went to Westminster Abbey. Six doors down the same street, Verne had just put a man who bet he could go round the world without looking at any of it. One end of a three-minute street: the people who wanted to see everything. The other end: a man who crosses the planet and notices nothing. The Society sold the building to a tailor in nineteen twelve — partly because that firm had dressed so many of the explorers.
